paragraph: Northvale is a single-family town first, with 19 detached sales over six months at a median of $770,000 and a sale-to-list ratio of 1.0013. Homes are moving quickly, a median of 16 days on market and one sale in four days, but the near-even ratio says buyers are paying close to ask rather than bidding prices up sharply. Competitive, not frenzied. The range runs from $535,000 to $1,490,000, so the median is the better guide than either end. Condos and townhouses are a thin second tier at 6 sales and a median of $655,000, with a median of 33 days on market and a ratio of exactly 1.00. That is a small enough count that you should treat it as a price reference point, not a trend. Every month in the series closed fewer than five single-family sales, so the month-to-month medians swing on mix alone and cannot carry a trend claim. If Northvale follows the usual Bergen seasonal arc, expect fall closings to drift below the summer numbers. If you are choosing between tiers here, it comes down to whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance setup of a townhouse.
